exposure: head-perineum distance at the initiation of the active second stage of labor
Head-perineum distance at the initiation of the active second stage of labor
outcome: Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. instrumental vaginal delivery or cesarean section)
cohort: 286 full-term parturients giving birth to newborns in cephalic presentation
finding: A head-perineum distance below 44 mm at the initiation of the active second stage of labor was predictive of vaginal delivery, with a higher risk of medical intervention (instrumental vaginal delivery or cesarean section) when the distance was greater than 44 mm.
